quality: Desire-first opening promise: Tower of God landing copy asks what the reader wants before explaining the world; Solo Leveling Vol. 1 copy names E-rank weakness and family bills before dungeon spectacle.
reader_effect: The first screen is repeatable in one sentence; the reader knows why to care before lore accumulates.
principle: Attach a personal want or humiliation to a spatial or rule machine in the opening unit; do not open on unexplained beauty.
our_handling: Ember Lattice story-bible and CH01 reader open inside Ember Vault with a live boss and printed LV/XP chrome. Borrowed Down lettered CH01-S01-P01 states 'In Veyr, down arrives by schedule' over a civic crane city. City Keeps Oaths CH01-S01-P01 stages an adult pathwright on a luminous road. All three have premises; only Borrowed Down puts the thesis in a single caption-plus-image beat.
gap_evidence: Ember P001 is a high-density void with tiny silhouettes; the want (class key / salvage debt) is overlay text, not body language. City's opening is scenic competence, not humiliation. Ember P024 source raster is a standing two-shot plus collapsed boss while the alt-text claims a class-choice hook.
original_direction: Storyboard the first two scroll units as: (1) a body that cannot yet do the job, (2) the original machine that will test that want. Ember: Elian's failed salvage posture on the chain before the vault beauty. Borrowed Down: Mae already carrying load. City: a road that fails under Sola's hand before the skyline.
prohibited_similarity: No 'What do you desire?' copy, tower-entry wish premise, E-rank hunter humiliation, hospital-bill raid framing, or named-title splash compositions.

quality: Hook speed: ToG lists Ep. 0 then 1F.Headon's Floor; Solo Leveling Vol. 1 contents move Prologue to Double Dungeon to Three Commandments to Quest; Tapas TBATE titles mana, sparring, ambush, and teamwork inside the first ten episodes; Tapas help prefers ~5-minute first episodes that still hook.
reader_effect: Readers can decide to continue after one commute unit; feedback loops start after one or two episodes rather than after a collected volume (SIU).
principle: The opening episode must complete one condition, one complication, and one unanswered vector without a lore preface.
our_handling: Ember CH01 plans P001-P004 setup and P005-P015 causal fight inside 24 panels, with end-state LV 4 printed in the reader. City and Borrowed Down ship ten full chapters but as equal-cell or equal-height stacks, not bite-size weekly episodes. Failure-correction contract requires each chapter to open with condition/objective and close on a consequential turn.
gap_evidence: All three pipelines produce volume-scale chapter dumps (24/30/24 panels) rather than 5-minute episode packets. Ember's hook is structurally present in the plan but visually delayed by painterly scale plates. City CH01 phone preview repeats medium-wide road tableaux before stakes sharpen.
original_direction: Compile a 12-18 unit 'episode 0' pack per pipeline: one want, one rule that changes a decision, one last-panel question. Do not wait for a 10-chapter volume to prove the hook.
prohibited_similarity: No Headon floor tests, double-dungeon raid structure, TBATE episode titles, or copied cliffhanger dialogue.

quality: Protagonist appeal starts as mismatch, not finished icon: ToG sells want versus tower; Solo Leveling sells the weakest hunter; unOrdinary sells the ignored student; Weak Hero sells small stature plus calculative fighting.
reader_effect: Readers track a body they can pity or underestimate; later power reads as change rather than default beauty.
principle: Design the lead's opening silhouette as an incomplete tool. Growth must alter posture, wear, and negative space.
our_handling: Ember specifies Level 3 failed salvager, hooked shortblade, frayed coat. Borrowed Down specifies Mae as municipal ropewright who takes every load. City specifies Sola as a solitary expert who must stop owning every repair. Visual bibles require adult silhouettes recognizable in solid black at small size (Borrowed Down 96 px).
gap_evidence: Ember CH01 contact sheet still presents a handsome illustration lead with drifting hair/coat; P024 standing pose looks already competent beside a dead boss. City CH01-S01-P01 is already poised and scenic. Ember visual-bible cel-line is not what the volume rasters do.
original_direction: Lock an opening-body sheet: slumped breath, damaged tool, one missing competence. Ban 'hero key visual' cameras until a documented state change. Keep Borrowed Down's load-bearing crouch as the house acting note.
prohibited_similarity: No Bam/Jinwoo/John/Gray likeness, dark-coat shadow monarch silhouette, hunter plate armor, or school-uniform antihero designs.

quality: Supporting-cast differentiation by battle or social verb: SIU ties ToG positions to football roles in a multicultural battle story; Solo Leveling Vol. 1 copy already splits a missing-arm leader from a collapsing healer.
reader_effect: Readers can parse a group fight or argument at phone size because each body is doing a different job.
principle: Give each recurring adult a unique verb, tool, and fear. Silhouette must survive solid-black reduction.
our_handling: Ember: Faultline Adept reads fractures; Bastion Lancer fixes orientation; Orin refines; Sable races. Borrowed Down: Mae braces/calculates leverage; Dax improvises with air-reads; Tavi calls community. City: Sola repairs routes; Tarin holds perimeter; Kesin records; Serac extracts unbounded vows. Visual bibles list hair anchors and kit.
gap_evidence: Ember volume rasters often pose Elian and Mira as matching illustration couple in similar three-quarter stances (CH01 P003/P018/P024 contact sheet). City grayscale CH01 repeats two-shot civic staging. Kit exists in prompts more reliably than in pixels.
original_direction: Storyboard group beats as verb diagrams before rendering: one braces, one reads, one calls. Reject any multi-character plate where two adults share stance, camera height, and hand occupation. Original verbs only.
prohibited_similarity: No fisherman/spear-bearer/light-bearer/scout/wave-controller labels, shinsu roles, hunter-class badges, or copied weapon silhouettes.

quality: Emotional stakes bound to survival economics or conflicting private needs, not abstract world-saving: Yen Press Vol. 1 names hospital bills, tuition, and no alternatives; SIU describes long-run anti-boredom via character chemistry that can diverge from the outline.
reader_effect: Danger is personal; a raid or test failure costs someone the reader already met.
principle: Every opening threat must invoice a relationship or a livelihood. Later spectacle spends that invoice.
our_handling: Ember: class key to leave salvage debt; Mira refuses sacrifice-as-strategy. Borrowed Down thesis: somebody carries the load; attraction is competence then consent. City: unbounded civic vows become tyranny; Sola must distribute obligation.
gap_evidence: Ember volume pictures still privilege dungeon beauty over the debt (P001 scale, CH10 boss key visual). City phone preview's early balloons are observation ('Every road in Caelune remembers') more than cost. Plans carry emotion; faces in generated plates often stay generic-serious.
original_direction: Require one close acting unit per episode where a choice about money, breath, consent, or load is visible in hands and brow, with no environment contest. Original adult relationships only.
prohibited_similarity: No Jinwoo family-hospital plot, Bam/Rachel betrayal configuration, or TBATE reincarnated-king loneliness replica.

quality: Mystery and future-vector that outlive the first boss: ToG keeps floor/rift titles across seasons; Solo Leveling copy withholds System origin and dungeon secrets; ORV hook is knowing the ending and changing it.
reader_effect: Chapter ends ask a new question instead of displaying a trophy.
principle: Close on a vector (unanswered want, new rule, social fracture), not on a posed victory.
our_handling: Ember CH01 P024 alt-text offers class choice before Bell Regent ascent; CH10 bible seals a fourth meridian. City CH10 restores a plural covenant and points outward. Borrowed Down CH10 kiss still preserves conflicting civic ambitions.
gap_evidence: Inspected Ember P024 raster is a victory tableau (two standing adults, collapsed Belljaw) with propulsion left to overlay. City CH01 last beats return to road-and-skyline beauty. Weekly last-panel meetings described by Sleepy-C are not a pipeline stage.
original_direction: Add a mandatory last-unit storyboard review: the picture itself must contain the question (a closed lift, a spent knot, a road that answers back). Overlay copy may name it but cannot be the only vector.
prohibited_similarity: No floor-guardian cliff, System-window cliff, constellation-scenario cliff, or copied 'next floor' structures.

quality: Progression visibility: Solo Leveling is classified video-game-related and promises exclusive leveling that applies to stronger enemies; ToG makes rank geographic (floors/tests); City/Ember bibles already prefer body-and-tool change over floating HUD.
reader_effect: Readers feel a scoreboard even when they skip menus, because the next fight looks different.
principle: Show increment, application, cost, and social reading of the gain. Menus are optional; wear and posture are not.
our_handling: Ember Brass Ledger requires four meaningful UI moments per chapter and maps to SystemState. City progression-bible shows witness/listen/hold/span/sever/chorus through bracer, coat, spear, badge. Borrowed Down shows knots charging, fraying, and scarring. Ember Phase B CH01-CH06 audit PASSes persistent XP, class, injuries, and loot arithmetic.
gap_evidence: Ledger is a post-composited SVG layer, not a decision posed in the acting. Ember volume rasters rarely show the stated HP/Qi/inventory cost on the body beyond a rib wrap. City's chords are sometimes indistinguishable glow. Borrowed Down's charged yellow saltglass is clearer but not sequentialized as weekly increments.
original_direction: For Ember, make the Ledger a diegetic brass plate in reserved negative space designed at storyboard, never a blue glass replica. For all pipelines, require a before/after body pair per chapter (posture, wear, tool) that a grayscale thumbnail can read.
prohibited_similarity: No blue holographic windows, hunter ranks, gates, shadow army, quest-log chrome, or copied numeric HUD layouts.

quality: Antagonist iconography as rank-and-function shape: ToG names floor tests in the episode list; Solo Leveling Vol. 1 promises a being whose power outranks the party; VFX Voice notes storyboards that emphasize beast size versus humans.
reader_effect: Opposition is memorable as a silhouette and a job, not as generic monster paint.
principle: Design antagonists as readable functions (tester, extractor, outranking presence) with one iconic mass and one weak-point rule.
our_handling: Ember Belljaw: ivory kiln shoulder, bell jaw, orange ankle seam, charge/clamp/wrench. Bell Regent: climbing bell torso. Borrowed Down keelbacks: whale-sized crescents, no evil teeth. City Serac: magistrate as negative mirror of Sola's competence-obligation.
gap_evidence: Belljaw scale and joint logic drift across Ember CH01 contact sheet (P004 vs P007 vs P024). CH10 P001 is a cinematic key visual more than a functional tester. City antagonists share coat-and-dusk staging with protagonists in the CH01 grayscale sheet. Creature-fail repair in Borrowed Down CH10-S04 shows the pipeline can still invent toothed anatomy against bible.
original_direction: Freeze one orthographic enemy sheet per boss (mass, verb, weak point, prohibited extra orifices). Reject plates that add menace-teeth or lose the job-shape. Keep Belljaw's bell-jaw and Mae's civic antagonists original.
prohibited_similarity: No statue-dungeon gods, ant-king, monarchs, Headon, Jahad family crests, or copied boss palettes.

quality: Quiet-to-spectacle contrast and swipe rhythm: CLIP STUDIO webtoon paneling stresses instant comprehension, contrast, and even balloon-only beats; SIU's long-run craft is not boring after first freshness; Sleepy-C budgets episode-final scenes as team highlights.
reader_effect: Spectacle lands because the eye was rested; readers keep scrolling instead of bouncing off texture.
principle: Precommit density. Never adjacent maximums. Use acting or balloon-only units as rest. Spend finish on the last beat of a fight, not on every establishing plate.
our_handling: Ember visual-bible and failure-correction contract: ≥65% low, quiet every four, no adjacent highs. Phase B CH01-CH06: 96/36/12. City density plan 16 low / 5 moderate / 3 high per 24. Borrowed Down sequence recipe: one T3, two T2, one T1 emotion, one T0/T1 breath when story allows.
gap_evidence: Ember P001 and CH10 P001 spend maximum finish on establishing illustration. City 186/240 metric WARN vs 29 manual PASS shows proxies and eyes disagree, but the phone preview still feels even-height cinematic. Borrowed Down later sheets are flagged dense at phone size. Balloon-only rest units are not in the generated art path.
original_direction: Author rest units as first-class ComicPanelPlan types (acting close, balloon-only, empty air). Generate those cheaper. Spend model budget on contact and last-panel propulsion only.
prohibited_similarity: No tracing of ToG/SL rest-to-splash page turns, ORV banquet layouts, or named-title climax boards.

quality: Vertical reveal as variable-height directing, not equal plates: WEBTOON/Naver/Kakao/Tapas serialize as continuous vertical mobile canvas; SIU notes Korean comics are web-first; Tapas features mobile-friendly vertical scroll.
reader_effect: The thumb discovers scale, then face, then impact; the reader feels timed, not tiled.
principle: Height is pacing. Full-bleed tall units for scale, short units for reaction, empty air before reveals. Equal grids fight the medium.
our_handling: Ember volume HTML is a continuous phone reader of 1024x1536 plates stacked. City assembles 24 similar-height panels per chapter. Borrowed Down uses 1x5 strips with letterboxed 4:3/1:1/3:4 roles — a partial attempt that still crops from equal sheets.
gap_evidence: City CH01 phone preview is a column of cinematic stills of nearly equal height. Ember P001 is tall but every neighbor is the same canvas. Borrowed Down bakes blank rectangles into every cell. None author a balloon-only short unit or a double-height impact the way native webtoon storyboards do. Licensed ToG/SL exact reveal timing is not_assessed.
original_direction: Replace equal-cell generation with a scroll score: each unit declares height class (breath/acting/action/scale). Assemble after, like lettering. Do not generate five-panel contact sheets as the directing format.
prohibited_similarity: No traced ToG tower-reveal crops, SL dungeon-drop crops, or uploaded licensed strips as layout references.

quality: Shot-size variation and camera as directing: CLIP STUDIO says webtoon panels are rarely studied in detail and must read at a glance; Sleepy-C art director explicitly directs pose, expression, lighting; Hashimoto-style storyboard practice (cited in prior Ember research) treats scripts through a camera lens. Licensed ToG/SL shot grammar is not_assessed at panel level.
reader_effect: The scroll breathes: scale, medium geography, close acting, impact. Sameness reads as slideshow.
principle: No three consecutive units may share shot size and camera height. Close-ups carry decisions; wides carry only new geography.
our_handling: Ember CH01 reader alts include scale (P001), profile (P002), faces (P003), extreme CU inventory (P013), and impact (P015) — the plan knows variation. City visual-bible: establish once, then simplify; close faces/hands for decisions. Borrowed Down: T0-T3 tiers.
gap_evidence: Ember CH01 contact sheet still clusters three-quarter mediums. City CH01 grayscale is dominated by medium-wide two-shots with the road as vanishing point. Borrowed Down 5-cell sheets force mixed sizes into one generation, then crop. Variation is a prompt hope, not a camera ledger.
original_direction: Add a shot-size field to ComicPanelPlan with fail-closed repetition checks. Generate closes and wides as separate requests so the model cannot average toward medium beauty.
prohibited_similarity: No recreation of signature ToG or SL camera angles, statue-room compositions, or named-artist lenses.

quality: Depth and value grouping: professional serials (studio interviews) treat lighting as atmosphere and focal rank; CLIP STUDIO recommends subtracting busy backgrounds; City grayscale evidence shows even midtones across many panels.
reader_effect: The eye hits one subject on a phone. Competing midtones cause skip.
principle: One dominant value break per ordinary unit. Brightest light, strongest saturation, sharpest edge belong to the narrative focal point.
our_handling: Ember palette: charcoal/ivory/teal/brass/ember-only accent. City: midnight/pearl with cyan-gold oathlight as sole accent. Borrowed Down: one dominant value break, paper as force, limited hatch. Ember grayscale diagnostics exist in volume and premium readers.
gap_evidence: Ember volume plates keep painterly atmospheric wash that equalizes figure and architecture (P001, P017, CH10 P001). City CH01 grayscale: similar figure-left/road-right luminance in P01-P06 and P12/P19/P24. Borrowed Down pressure-print is the only pipeline whose value break is graphically intentional, and even it drifts toward polished illustration (style-probe review).
original_direction: Gate ordinary panels on a grayscale thumbnail test: if two regions compete at 390 px, simplify. Keep ember/oathlight/yellow-cord as the single accent family per title. Do not solve grouping by adding more paint.
prohibited_similarity: No Solo Leveling dungeon-blue rims, ToG shinsu glows, or copied lighting recipes.

quality: Line and shape confidence versus painterly convergence: Ember style-candidate review selected angular contour against soft painterly C; Borrowed Down selected pressure-print; City selected clean cinematic. Licensed ToG/SL line weight is not_assessed; Disciples publicly pledged to keep DUBU's mise-en-scene, structure, and drawing quality.
reader_effect: Confident contour reads as sequential art; soft full-frame paint reads as AI key visual even when composition is decent.
principle: House contour is a production constraint, not a flavor adjective. If the raster cannot hold the contour, the route failed regardless of beauty.
our_handling: Ember visual-bible: tapered charcoal, limited interiors, two-step cel. Borrowed Down: thick dry-brush keyline, spot inks. City: crisp dark-navy contours, limited interiors. All three still generate through a general image model with text-free prompts.
gap_evidence: Ember P007 cream-void action and P001 dungeon volume do not share a contour system. CH10 P001 is 3D-cinematic metal. City opening plate is smooth painterly fantasy despite 'clean cinematic' lock. Borrowed Down style-probe review already notes drift toward polished illustration rather than cheap-print registration.
original_direction: Fail any plate that loses the house edge language, even if identity is correct. Prefer fewer, locally edited contour-true panels over ten-chapter painterly volume. Borrowed Down's tactile edge is the existence proof that a constrained ink logic can survive generation better than 'premium cel' adjectives.
prohibited_similarity: No requests for DUBU, SIU, Sleepy-C, uru-chan, RAZEN, or any living artist's line; no title-style prompts.

quality: Anatomy, acting, and hands as directed craft: Le Monde/Disciples and Sleepy-C both treat pose and expression as studio-directed; Cartoon Brew notes amateur-to-capable fight flow as an explicit study target in the SL adaptation. Licensed manhwa hands/anatomy are not_assessed at panel-forensic level.
reader_effect: Believable grip and face acting make impact and emotion cheap; broken hands make readers distrust the fight.
principle: Storyboard footing, grip, contact, and brow before rendering. Hands doing the job outrank facial beauty.
our_handling: Ember action bible specifies footing, attack vector, grip, contact, consequence. Borrowed Down visual-bible: large readable hands, grounded feet, brow/jaw/shoulder acting. City: close faces, hands, tools, posture carry decisions. Premium Ember editorial redirected balloon tails when two-shots confused speakers — acting ownership was a lettering problem too.
gap_evidence: Ember P007 spear grip is among the better hands, but CH01 contact sheet shows softened fists, drifting anatomy, and repeated three-quarter faces. City acting is elegant and low-range (same profile, same dusk). Borrowed Down strongest rope-grip panel works; equal-grid neighbors do not all keep that standard. No pipeline has a human pose-pass equivalent to REDICE drawing teams.
original_direction: Add a hands/footing assertion to action panels and reject plates that fail it before lettering. Use localized repair on grip/contact only. Do not imitate any named artist's acting library.
prohibited_similarity: No uploaded licensed panels as pose references; no named-artist acting; no Jinwoo amateur-brawler choreography copies.

quality: Costume and weapon as state, not fashion: SL's public arc is a body that changes as it levels; City and Borrowed Down bibles already encode coat cuts, knots, spears, badges; Ember tracks cracked rib, bent spear, consumed talismans.
reader_effect: Readers can reread a silhouette and know the chapter. Wardrobe becomes memory.
principle: Irreversible wear is the cheap progression UI. If the coat is identical after a boss, the fight did not happen.
our_handling: Ember continuity: injuries, consumed materials, repaired gear persist (Phase B audit PASS). Borrowed Down: Mae sleeve tear, Dax cape states, used knots gray. City: Sola sleeve cut CH04, copper bracer break CH08, Tarin spear bend/shatter.
gap_evidence: Ember CH01 P024 still shows relatively intact coats after a boss that cracked a rib; identity drift fights the wear ledger. City CH01 phone preview does not yet show the later coat surgery. Generated models prefer pristine hero cloth.
original_direction: Bind a wear atlas into every prompt and fail-closed check: tears, wraps, fray, spent knots. Prefer one dirty original coat to a new 'upgraded' fantasy outfit. No hunter-cloak evolution path.
prohibited_similarity: No shadow-monarch wardrobe, hunter guild uniforms, ToG ranker cloaks, or TBATE mana-core fashion.

quality: Color-script as scene tone, not rainbow: Yen Press markets SL as full-color; Sleepy-C directs lighting; our bibles already lock accent families. Licensed scene-by-scene palettes are not_assessed.
reader_effect: Color tells the reader where they are and what is dangerous without a caption.
principle: One accent family per title. Environment shifts hue; the accent is reserved for state change.
our_handling: Ember: ember-orange only luminous accent; Ledger brass. Borrowed Down: chapter-phased teal/coral/yellow. City: cyan-gold oathlight, black-gold fracture only for corruption.
gap_evidence: Ember volume lighting still invents extra rim glow and metallic spec. City dusk palettes flatten difference between ordinary and crisis panels. Borrowed Down is the most script-obedient and still drifts toward extra polish.
original_direction: Per-chapter color board with forbidden extra accents. Grayscale-first review. Ember must not grow a second magic color to imitate SL full-color richness.
prohibited_similarity: No SL blue System, purple monarch, ToG shinsu aqua, or ORV constellation gold replicas.

quality: Effects hierarchy: one family at contact, then aftermath. Licensed ToG/SL effect recipes are not_assessed; CLIP STUDIO warns dense backgrounds interrupt swipe flow; Ember bible already limits debris and speed wedges to contact.
reader_effect: The blow is readable. Stacked glows hide who hit whom.
principle: Effects are punctuation. Ordinary panels get none. Contact gets one family. Aftermath is changed posture, not leftover particles.
our_handling: Ember: reserve debris/speed wedges for contact; one effect family in low-detail. City: no stacked competing effects. Borrowed Down: motion as displaced ink, catenaries, spray — not generic speed lines.
gap_evidence: Ember P014 ember ring and CH10 metallic volume compete with environment glow. City oathlight often blankets hands. Generator default is 'more VFX = more epic,' the opposite of the bibles.
original_direction: Hard-cap effect families in the panel plan. Composite effects locally (already a North Garden research direction) instead of asking the image model to invent them.
prohibited_similarity: No SL dagger-aura, shadow-burst, ToG shinsu bangs, or copied SFX shapes.

quality: Attack / counter / reversal grammar: Ember action bible already writes geography → charge → initiate → clamp → read → move → backhand → consequence → sacrifice → breakthrough → combo. Cartoon Brew records SL adaptation staff studying amateur-to-capable flow. Licensed manhwa beat-by-beat reversal is not_assessed.
reader_effect: Readers understand who is winning without a narrator. A reversal feels earned.
principle: Every fight unit must change occupancy, grip, or injury. A pretty clash with unchanged bodies is not a fight.
our_handling: Ember Phase B CH03-CH04 audit PASSes Glassback and Bailiff sequences for intention, contact, consequence, adaptation. Failure-correction contract requires that chain. Borrowed Down: footing, taut line, load source, contact, remaining consequence. City: constraint → contact → choice → consequence.
gap_evidence: Ember CH01 contact sheet still contains illustration poses that do not obviously continue screen direction (P007 cream void vs P006 dungeon). City CH01 phone preview's 'KRAK' pylon beat is a single splash among similar two-shots, not a reversal chain. Pipeline tests arithmetic more than occupancy.
original_direction: Require a fight strip proof (6-8 units) in grayscale before full color. Screen-direction and occupancy assertions fail-closed. Keep Ember's original Fault-read versus Mira-pin combo; do not borrow SL's dagger tempo.
prohibited_similarity: No statue-commandment trials, Jinwoo dagger strings, ToG position-team set pieces, or Weak Hero school-fight blocking copies.

quality: Scale and environment as premise, not wallpaper: SIU describes the tower as hierarchical closed space; SL publisher and storyboard reporting emphasize outranking beasts; Ember P001 and Borrowed Down crane-city and City cloud-road all attempt this.
reader_effect: The world feels larger than the lead. Danger has architecture.
principle: Establish geography once with a readable human measure, then simplify. Scale panels need a tiny body and a job, not infinite texture.
our_handling: Ember Hollow Meridian is descending ribs and chains; ordinary panels should simplify to one arch/chain/gradient. Borrowed Down Serein Sea is a continent-high wall with civic keels. City Caelune is crescents over a cloud sea. All three bibles forbid equal detail everywhere.
gap_evidence: Ember P001 and CH10 P001 over-render stone/metal so the human measure nearly vanishes. City roads are beautiful and repetitive. Borrowed Down opening scale works, then later equal-grid cells cannot keep environmental ambition without density failure.
original_direction: One scale unit per episode maximum, with a measured human pixel height. Follow-ups reuse a simplified set plate. Original architecture only: chains/keels/oathglass, never a tower of tests or hunter gates.
prohibited_similarity: No ToG tower exterior, inner-floor test rooms, SL gates/dungeons/statues, or ORV subway map.

quality: Balloons, SFX, and UI as directing layers: Yen Press credits a dedicated SL letterer; TBATE Season 7 credits letters, QC, and editors separately; Tapas/CLIP STUDIO require mobile-legible type and tails; our pipelines composite locally but often outside or on top of unplanned art.
reader_effect: Readers hear who speaks and what changed without covering the blow. UI feels like a world object, not a video-game sticker.
principle: Reserve negative space in the storyboard. Dialogue, SFX, and system chrome have different shapes. Phone type has a floor.
our_handling: Ember v2 lettering bible: soft/open/butted/linked balloons, Brass Ledger components, 15 CSS px floor, 26-38% width. Premium editorial moved tails (P033) and UI off faces (P034). Borrowed Down: cream balloons with coral ticks, but caption bands under art and baked blank rectangles. City: deterministic balloons; seven lettering-only repairs; art unchanged.
gap_evidence: Ember CH01 P001 SVG is a large 76% opaque caption card over the scale shot. Borrowed Down CH01-S01-P01 keeps a huge empty rectangle in the artwork plus an exterior caption. City CH01 phone preview uses small pills that sometimes sit on faces; SFX are sparse (KRAK, TIK, SSSSK). None integrate SFX into contour the way a weekly webtoon lettering pass would. Licensed ToG/SL balloon geometry is not_assessed.
original_direction: Design lettering voids as composition, not as baked boxes. Ember Ledger stays brass/cut-corner and diegetic. Borrowed Down should retire the under-art caption band. Never copy blue System windows or ToG balloon styling.
prohibited_similarity: No SL System chrome, ToG balloon/SFX style, ORV scenario windows, or uploaded lettering references.

quality: Chapter-end propulsion as a budgeted picture: Sleepy-C says the final scene of every episode is a team meeting; ToG/SL keep weekly cadences (Monday on WEBTOON/Tappytoon); Tapas wants the first episode to hook while remaining short.
reader_effect: The thumb stops on a question. Next-week desire is visual.
principle: Last unit is the most expensive directing beat, not leftover copy on a victory pose.
our_handling: Ember failure-correction contract: each chapter closes on a consequential turn. CH01 P024 is intended as class-choice + Bell Regent clock. City chapters end on covenant questions. Borrowed Down CH10 preserves conflicting ambitions after the kiss.
gap_evidence: Ember P024 picture is a trophy pose; the question is in the overlay. No pipeline has an episode-end review meeting analogous to REDICE. Ten-chapter volumes substitute for weekly last-panel craft.
original_direction: Create an explicit last-unit checklist: unanswered want visible in image, no trophy pose unless the trophy is dangerous, overlay may label but not invent the hook. Ship episode packets, not only volumes.
prohibited_similarity: No copied ToG/SL/ORV cliff compositions or dialogue.

quality: Production evolution and QC: SIU serialized from 2010 with later assistants; SL continued from DUBU to DISCIPLES with an explicit staging/structure/drawing standard (Le Monde); ORV/REDICE uses storyboard, 3D materials, split drawing/color/bg/polish teams; TBATE lists QC and letters. Our pipelines log hashes and repairs but do not own a pose QC role.
reader_effect: Weekly finish stays readable because humans specialize. Succession does not collapse the house staging.
principle: Storyboard is the directing record. Specialized QC of pose, contact, and last panel beats any aggregate beauty score. Finish may evolve; grammar must not.
our_handling: All three pipelines separate ComicPanelPlan from RenderRecord, keep lettering local, isolate repairs (Borrowed Down hash-proof repairs; City lettering-only repairs; Ember P016 outdoor-continuity repair). Ember premium-rd recommends hybrid: structured plans, localized edit, SVG lettering. North Garden research has assertion manifests, but these reimaginings still accept unaccepted generated candidates as volume art.
gap_evidence: Owner-review-pending is the actual QC state. City repaired lettering and left art. Ember selected a contour candidate then produced painterly volumes. No storyboard artist role exists; the image model is asked to invent camera, acting, and effects together. That is the inverse of Sleepy-C's split.
original_direction: Insert a human or constrained-layout storyboard stage that owns camera, occupancy, and lettering voids before any raster. Limit the generator to filling approved shapes. Keep Ember's original world. Do not staff-cosplay REDICE or name their artists in prompts.
prohibited_similarity: No imitation of DUBU/Disciples/Sleepy-C/SIU drawing; no reuse of their 3D model look; no title-specific production assets.

quality: Simpler-art serialization can outrun hyper-render: unOrdinary and Weak Hero official copy sell social hierarchy, secret past, and calculative fighting; CLIP STUDIO says swipe rhythm beats detailed backgrounds; SIU's own early military drafts were practice quantity before polish.
reader_effect: Readers subscribe to character and question. Finish can grow later; unclear acting cannot.
principle: If contour, acting, and last-panel question are strong, reduced rendering is a feature. Do not spend the budget making every unit a key visual.
our_handling: Borrowed Down pressure-print is the repository's simpler, more original finish and scored highest in its style probe for identity/hands/environment. Ember and City chased cleaner/cinematic premium and converged toward generic paint. Ember failure-correction contract already warns against generic style convergence and named-source translation failure.
gap_evidence: City's 'clean cinematic' and Ember's 'premium cel' still look like illustration averages. Borrowed Down's best panels prove a constrained ink logic, but the equal-grid and caption band prevent it from reading as a native webtoon serial. We currently optimize for volume completeness, not weekly acting.
original_direction: Pilot a low-finish Ember or Borrowed Down episode pack: confident contour, six causal action beats, one close acting rest, one last-panel question, no extra texture. Measure phone comprehension, not gloss. Finish may rise later the way long-running official serials did, without copying their later look.
prohibited_similarity: No unOrdinary/Weak Hero casts, uniforms, power-copying, or bully-arc structures; no early-ToG tracing as a 'simpler' shortcut.
